newsitem.title: INDIA: India metals prices rise as state firms up rates.
newsitem.headline: India metals prices rise as state firms up rates.

text.p: Indian copper and zinc prices rose on Monday after state agencies raised their selling prices for February, dealers said. Nickel too gained on continued support.
"Copper and zinc climbed up on news that state-owned agencies have hiked selling prices for February," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
Ready copper rose by 100 rupees to 12,950 rupees per quintal and ready zinc rose by 50 to 6,900 rupees per quintal. Last week copper and zinc were up by 100 rupees each.
Dealers said state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd raised the selling prices of copper wire bar and copper cathodes by 4,000 rupees per tonne and of copper rod by 9,000 rupees per tonne for Feburary.
"Likewise Hindustan Zinc Ltd has also hiked selling prices of zinc by 1,500 rupees per tonne for February, but kept prices of lead unchanged," one dealer said.

Nickel rose by 100 rupees to 36,900 rupees per quintal on continued support while supplies were low. Nickel was up by 300 rupees last week. Lead was steady at 4,550 rupees, aluminium at 7,250 rupees and tin at 34,400 rupees amid restricted activity.
